title: Data visualization / Charts

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; visible default tab states

slide_intent: Choose a chart according to the comparison a person needs to make so visual form supports the question rather than merely decorating data.
strategic_value: A shared taxonomy of chart purposes can make IBM information displays more consistent and easier to interpret across contexts.
demonstration: Six sections group blue chart thumbnails by comparisons, trends, part-to-whole, correlations, relationships and connections, and maps, with names and implementation links.
practical_value: Match a data question to a chart family and compare the specific alternatives within that family.

content_islands.name: Comparisons
content_islands.spec: Begin the chart catalog with a grid of bars, lollipop, bubble, radar and word-cloud specimens under the comparison rationale.

content_islands.name: Trends
content_islands.spec: Follow with line, area, boxplot, histogram and stream examples tied to change over time.

content_islands.name: Part to whole
content_islands.spec: Place circular, stacked and nested shapes together to compare ways to express subdivision.

content_islands.name: Correlations
content_islands.spec: Group scatterplot, heatmap and parallel coordinates under multidimensional comparison.

content_islands.name: Relationships and maps
content_islands.spec: Close with flow/network/tree specimens followed by choropleth, proportional-symbol and connecting-line maps; preserve design-only labels where shown.

reference_purposes.Intent: Each section explains the perceptual or informational reason to use its family, such as alignment for comparison or position for geographic patterns.
reference_purposes.Expression: The specimen cards use a coordinated blue visual treatment across many chart structures.
reference_purposes.Application: Named examples and contextual descriptions help match comparison, trend, composition, correlation, relationship or geographic questions to chart types.
